title: Web UI: auto-mark article read after dwelling in the reader for WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS (default 5s)
description:
FEATURE (web UI — packages/aggregator-web/, HTMX + Alpine.js; NOT the TUI)
Automatically mark an article as read once it has been OPEN in the reader pane for a configurable dwell time (default 5 seconds). Motivation: the user skims an opened article for a few seconds and moves on, but without pressing 'm'/'n' it stays unread and clutters the Unread filter. This adds a client-side dwell timer that reuses the EXISTING read endpoint so all read indicators update dynamically. Purely additive; must not change any existing behavior.

CONFIG (one backend touch only)
Add a new web setting WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS (on the web service Settings subclass; WEB_ prefix), integer seconds, DEFAULT 5. Value 0 DISABLES the feature entirely (no timer wiring emitted / timer never armed). Inject this value into the page so the client JS can read it (e.g. render it into a data-* attribute on a stable element such as <body>/app root, or a small inline JS global in shell.html — follow however other WEB_* values are already surfaced to the client if any). Document the new var in CLAUDE.md's web settings table and in .env.example if that is where such vars live.

BEHAVIOR (client-side, in static/app.js within the aggregatorApp component)
Reader open flow today: _loadReader(id) does htmx.ajax GET on the URL "/article/<id>" into #reader-content and adds body.reader-open (app.js:278-288). The swapped-in #article-detail carries data-article-id and an is-read class. Manual read is _toggleOpenArticleRead()/_markReadAndNext() (app.js:60-83), which call htmx.ajax POST on "/article/<id>/read" (or "/unread") with { target:'#article-detail', swap:'outerHTML' }. The read route (app.py:212-233) returns the refreshed #article-detail PLUS the matching _article_card.html rendered oob=True (hx-swap-oob) AND sets HX-Trigger: refreshSidebar — so the read/unread round indicator on both the card and the detail, and the sidebar counts, all update live.

Implement auto-read as:
1. Read WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS on load. If 0, do nothing (feature off).
2. When an #article-detail is present/swapped into the reader AND it does NOT have the is-read class, ARM a dwell timer for that article id. Good hook points: the existing reader-content htmx:afterSwap (see app.js:286 where scrollTop is reset), or an equivalent afterSwap/observer on #reader-content — arm the timer there after confirming #article-detail exists and lacks is-read.
3. Only accumulate DWELL TIME WHILE THE TAB IS VISIBLE. Use the Page Visibility API (document.hidden / visibilitychange): pause accumulation when hidden, resume when visible. Do NOT reset progress on a brief tab switch — accumulate visible elapsed time so a quick switch away and back does not lose progress and does not falsely fire while hidden. (A timestamp-accumulator or a paused/resumed timer are both acceptable as long as only visible time counts.)
4. When accumulated visible time reaches WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS, fire the SAME request the manual path uses:
     htmx.ajax POST on the URL "/article/<id>/read" with { target: '#article-detail', swap: 'outerHTML' }
   where <id> is the open article's data-article-id. This MUST be the htmx.ajax call with target #article-detail (NOT a bare fetch), so the OOB card swap + the refreshSidebar HX-Trigger run and every read indicator (list card round indicator, reader detail, sidebar counts) updates dynamically. One-shot per open.
5. CANCEL / disarm the pending timer when any of these happen before it fires: the reader closes (reader:closed event / body loses reader-open — see closeReader app.js:86-89), a DIFFERENT article loads into the reader (next afterSwap — re-arm for the new article), or the user manually marks the article read via m/n (avoid a double POST). If the open article is already is-read on load, do not arm.
6. Applies uniformly wherever the reader shows an article — normal feed views AND thread-member articles (both load #article-detail into #reader-content). Do NOT arm for the BRIEF reader (briefs are not read/unread articles); ensure the timer only arms when an #article-detail with data-article-id is present, which naturally excludes briefs.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT change existing keyboard shortcuts, manual read/unread, or any other behavior. Additive only.
- No new backend read endpoint — reuse the existing POST "/article/<id>/read" exactly as the m key does.
- Never fire while the tab is hidden; never fire more than once per open; never fire for an already-read article or a brief.
- If WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS=0 the feature is fully off (no timers armed).

REGRESSION / VERIFICATION
- Automated (pytest, testable): assert the web app exposes WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS with default 5; assert the rendered page surfaces the configured value to the client (the chosen data attribute / inline global is present with the value), and that when set to 0 the page reflects the disabled state (value 0 present) so the JS gate has something to test against. Add/adjust a settings test for the new field and its default.
- The dwell-timer + visibility behavior itself is client-side JS and is NOT unit-testable in this package (Alpine/JS has no test harness here). State clearly in the handoff that BROWSER VERIFICATION is required: open an unread article and wait 5s without interacting -> it becomes read (card round indicator flips, sidebar unread count drops) while the reader stays open; open and close within <5s -> stays unread; open, switch browser tabs before 5s of visible time, come back -> only visible time counts; set WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS=0 -> nothing auto-marks; confirm manual m/n and 'v'/'c' still work.

FILES: packages/aggregator-web/src/aggregator_web/static/app.js (timer logic), the web service Settings subclass (new WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS field), packages/aggregator-web/src/aggregator_web/templates/shell.html (surface value to client), CLAUDE.md (web settings table), .env.example if present. Reference: app.py:212-233 (read route OOB swap), app.js:60-83 (manual read), app.js:278-288 (reader load), app.js:86-89 (closeReader).
